analysis:
The supplied units are head-text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 4074-4931). The only recorded change is documentation: file_changes shows one added paragraph at head lines 1561-1569, describing ByteFallbackDecoder trailing `<0xHH>` token handling in LocalTokenizerBridge.decode. That range lies outside the supplied units, so I could not verify it. The supplied excerpts are unchanged surrounding context, and nothing in them is a changed security control.

The context describes bounds already in place: authenticated-record limits (64 MiB array, 16 MiB raw frame, 8 MiB record plaintext), fail-closed refusal with no raw fallback, the cluster SSD prefix record encoding bound by a sealed header and load agreement, and a per-request memory budget. It also describes GPT-OSS, MiMo, Gemma and Nemotron batch and arithmetic bindings in the load agreement, plus content-free observation logs. These are descriptive of existing behavior, and no code change is supplied that weakens them.

The cluster SSD prefix records relate to T-041, the retained cache threat. The text says records are sealed with an encoding header and are deleted when of a foreign encoding, so the doc is consistent with that threat's at-rest posture. The statement that log records carry no token IDs, logits or prompt text is consistent with A-001 confidentiality.

No code is changed, so no regression, new attack surface or invalidated assumption can be demonstrated. Remaining questions for integration: the ByteFallbackDecoder paragraph at head line 1561 is not in the units I saw, and whether the doc claims match the source behavior (LocalTokenizerLoader, cluster runtime) is unverified. The claim that decode releases trailing byte-fallback runs could affect incremental detokenization output but not confidentiality from the doc alone.
